header.title: Demonstratio Evangelica: AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Eusebius of Caesarea
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's tlg2018.tlg005.1st1K-grc1, from Open Greek and Latin's First1KGreek (CC BY-SA 4.0), one English line for each line of the original. nodes.text: Again, we must turn to the opponent [and ask] whether he has ever seen with his eyes, or learned by hearsay, of sorcerers and poisoners practising sorcery without libations and sacrifices and the invocation and presence of demons. Can anyone, then, bring any such charge against our Saviour, or against his words, or against those who even now emulate his life? Is it not plain even to a blind man that we who are of Jesus' mind practise the very opposite of these things, daring to give up our souls to death sooner than [give] a sacrifice to demons, and departing from life sooner than submitting to be enslaved to the wicked demons?
